extracted.intended_audience: applicants, patent attorneys/agents, national Offices, International Searching Authorities and International Preliminary Examining Authorities operating under the PCT
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural standards governing the filing, transmittal, correction, conduct and reporting of international preliminary examination (IPE) under the Patent Cooperation Treaty (PCT), aimed at applicants and examinating authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmittal of the demand to the competent International Preliminary Examining Authority
rubrics_metrics.description: If a demand is submitted to a receiving Office, ISA or IPEA that is not competent, that Office/Authority shall mark the date of receipt and promptly transmit the demand to the International Bureau unless it proceeds under paragraph (f). If submitted to the International Bureau, the IB marks the date and transmits or invites the applicant to indicate the competent IPEA where two or more are competent; if no indication is furnished the demand is considered not submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IB must promptly transmit; where only one competent IPEA exists IB transmits and informs applicant; where multiple exist IB invites applicant to indicate within the applicable time limit (Rule 54 bis.1(a) or 15 days from invitation, whichever later); if applicant indicates, IB transmits to that IPEA; the date marked under receipt is the date of receipt for the competent IPEA. If an Office chooses to transmit directly to competent IPEA, paragraphs (c)–(e) apply mutatis mutandis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of defects in the demand (Rule 60.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the demand does not comply with specified requirements (Rules 53.1, 53.2, 53.3–53.8, 55.1), the IPEA shall invite the applicant to correct defects within a reasonable time limit, not less than one month from date of invitation; time limit may be extended before a decision is taken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant complies within the time limit, the demand is considered received on the actual filing date provided the demand permitted identification; otherwise considered received on date IPEA receives correction. If applicant fails to comply, the demand is treated as not submitted and IPEA declares so. If defect noticed by IB it brings to IPEA's attention. Special rules: (a-bis) and (a-ter) on multiple applicants (sufficient that certain indications or a signature provided by one applicant who has right to make demand). Paragraphs (f) and (g) cover absent statements concerning amendments and missing Article 34 amendments indicated in the statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of the demand and elections (Rule 61)
rubrics_metrics.description: IPEA shall indicate date of receipt on the demand, send or copy the demand to the International Bureau, and promptly notify the applicant of the date of receipt. The International Bureau effects notification to elected Offices under Article 31(7) and informs applicant of elected Offices notified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification to elected Offices must include application number, filing date, applicant name, priority filing date (if claimed) and date of receipt of demand by IPEA; notification is sent together with Article 20 communication. IB must publish information on the demand and elected States in the Gazette after filing the demand but not before international publication of the application. If demand considered as not submitted (per certain rules), IPEA notifies applicant and IB accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmission of ISA written opinion and Article 19 amendments to IPEA (Rule 62.1–62.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt of a demand or copy, the International Bureau shall promptly transmit to the IPEA a copy of the ISA's written opinion (Rule 43 bis.1) and copies of any Article 19 amendments, statements referred to in Article 19, and the Rule 46.5(b) letter, unless IPEA already received them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Article 19 amendments are filed after the demand, applicant should preferably simultaneously file copies with the IPEA; in any case the IB shall promptly transmit such amendments/statements/letters to the IPEA. IPEA shall promptly notify applicant of date of receipt of the demand and related materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation of ISA written opinion for the IPEA (Rule 62 bis.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon request of the IPEA, the ISA written opinion (when not in English or a language accepted by the IPEA) shall be translated into English by or under responsibility of the International Bureau.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IB must transmit translation to IPEA within two months of request and simultaneously transmit a copy to the applicant. Applicant may submit written observations on correctness of the translation and must send copies to both IPEA and IB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum requirements for International Preliminary Examining Authorities (Rule 63.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Minimum requirements (Article 32(3)) for an IPEA: (i) at least 100 full-time employees with sufficient technical qualifications; (ii) ready access to minimum documentation referred to in Rule 34, properly arranged; (iii) staff capable of examining required technical fields and language facilities to understand languages of the minimum documentation; (iv) a quality management system and internal review arrangements in accordance with common rules of international preliminary examination; (v) must hold appointment as an International Searching Authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are cumulative conditions establishing institutional capacity and resources required of a body to act as IPEA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of prior art for international preliminary examination (Rule 64.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: For Article 33(2) and (3) purposes, everything made available to the public anywhere in the world by means of written disclosure (including drawings and illustrations) prior to the relevant date shall be considered prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 'relevant date' is normally the international filing date of the international application under IPE (subject to priority rules); where priority is claimed and international filing date within priority period, the earlier filing date is the relevant date unless priority claim is considered invalid; special rule for claims where international filing date is after priority expiration but within two months (subject to IPEA view on priority claim validity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of non-written disclosures and certain published documents (Rule 64.2–64.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-written disclosures (oral disclosure, use, exhibition or other non-written means) before the relevant date are not considered prior art if their date is only indicated in a written disclosure made public on or after the relevant date; however the international preliminary examination report shall call attention to such non-written disclosures. Similarly, certain applications/patents filed earlier but published on or after the relevant date are not treated as prior art but must be called to attention in the report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPE report must note such non-written disclosures (Rule 70.9) and such published applications/patents (Rule 70.10) even where they are not considered prior art for Article 33(2) and (3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach to inventive step (non-obviousness) assessment (Rule 65.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: International preliminary examination shall consider the relation of any particular claim to the prior art as a whole, including combinations of documents or parts of documents where such combinations are obvious to a person skilled in the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must assess claims not only against individual documents but also against combinations; the relevant date for inventive step is the date prescribed in Rule 64.1 (priority/international filing date rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis and scope of international preliminary examination (Rule 66.1 and related)
rubrics_metrics.description: IPE shall be based on the international application as filed, subject to amendments under Article 34 (which may be submitted at time of filing the demand or up to establishment of report), and Article 19 amendments made before or after the demand, unless superseded. Rectification of obvious mistakes authorized under Rule 91.1 may be taken into account. Claims lacking an international search report need not be the subject of IPE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments under Article 19 made before the demand are generally taken into account unless superseded; amendments after the demand and Article 34 submissions are taken into account subject to timing rules (see Rule 66.4 bis).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of ISA written opinion by IPEA and notifications (Rule 66.1 bis)
rubrics_metrics.description: The ISA written opinion established under Rule 43 bis.1 is to be considered a written opinion of the IPEA for purposes of Rule 66.2(a), subject to exceptions. An IPEA may notify the IB that this will not apply to written opinions by specified ISAs; IB shall publish such notifications in the Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where an IPEA notifies that ISA written opinions by certain ISAs will not apply, the IPEA must notify the applicant. Even where not considered a written opinion for Rule 66.2(a), the ISA written opinion shall nevertheless be taken into account by the IPEA in proceeding under Rule 66.2(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Top-up searches by the IPEA (Rule 66.1 ter)
rubrics_metrics.description: The IPEA shall conduct a top-up search to discover documents (as per Rule 64) published or made available to it for search after the international search report was established, unless it considers such search would serve no useful purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the IPEA finds that situations referred to in Article 34(3) or (4) or Rule 66.1(e) exist, the top-up search shall cover only those parts of the international application that are the subject of IPE. IPEA exercises discretion whether top-up search is useful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content and notification procedure for the IPEA's written opinion (Rule 66.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: IPEA must notify the applicant in writing where it: (i) considers situations referred to in Article 34(4) exist; (ii) considers any claim should be negative for lack of novelty, inventive step or industrial applicability; (iii) notices defects in form/contents under the Treaty/Regulations; (iv) considers any amendment goes beyond the disclosure as filed; (v) wishes to accompany the report by observations on clarity/support; (vi) considers a claim relates to an invention without an ISR and decides not to examine it; (vii) cannot meaningfully examine due to unavailable nucleotide/amino acid sequence listing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notification must fully state reasons, invite written reply (with amendments where appropriate), and fix a reasonable time limit for reply — normally two months after notification, not less than one month, at least two months if ISR is transmitted simultaneously, and not more than three months unless extended. Time limit may be extended on applicant's request before expiration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant's formal response to IPEA written opinion (Rule 66.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may respond to IPEA's invitation by submitting amendments, or, if disagreeing, by submitting arguments, or both. Any response shall be submitted directly to the IPEA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responses should address the reasons stated in the notification and may include claim amendments or arguments as appropriate; direct filing to IPEA is required (not via IB).

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional opportunities to submit amendments or arguments (Rule 66.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: IPEA may issue one or more additional written opinions; Rules 66.2 and 66.3 apply to such opinions. On applicant's request, IPEA may give one or more additional opportunities to submit amendments or arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides discretionary iterative examination process; applicant can request further opportunities and IPEA can grant them subject to procedure rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for consideration of amendments, arguments and rectifications (Rule 66.4 bis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments, arguments and rectifications of obvious mistakes need not be taken into account by IPEA for purposes of a written opinion or the report if received by, authorized by or notified to the IPEA after it has begun to draw up that opinion or report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPEA may disregard late submissions made after drafting has started; applicants should file timely to ensure consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of amendment for IPE purposes (Rule 66.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any change, other than rectification of an obvious mistake, in the claims, description, or drawings (including cancellation of claims, omission of passages or drawings) shall be considered an amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rectifications of obvious mistakes are explicitly excluded from being treated as amendments; other changes trigger amendment procedures and requirements (form, basis statements, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Informal communications between IPEA and applicant (Rule 66.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: IPEA may at any time communicate informally with the applicant by telephone, in writing, or through personal interviews, and may decide at its discretion whether to grant more than one personal interview or to reply to informal written communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Informal communications are permitted but are discretionary; multiple interviews are at IPEA's discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of priority documents and translations (Rule 66.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: If IPEA needs a copy of the earlier application whose priority is claimed, the IB shall furnish it on request. If not furnished because applicant failed Rule 17.1 requirements and the earlier application is not otherwise available, the report may be established as if priority had not been claimed. If the priority application is in a different language, IPEA may invite applicant to furnish a translation within two months where validity of the priority claim is relevant; failure may result in report as if priority not claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures IPEA can assess priority validity; applicant must supply copies/translations when requested to avoid adverse treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and presentation requirements for amendments (Rule 66.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: When amending description or drawings, applicant generally must submit replacement sheets for every sheet that differs, accompanied by a letter highlighting differences, indicating the basis for amendment in the application as filed and preferably explaining reasons. Deletions or minor changes may use copies provided clarity is maintained. Claims amendments follow Rule 46.5 mutatis mutandis and the submitted set replaces all previously filed claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replacement sheets must be directly reproducible and accompanied by basis explanation (Rule 46.5(b)(iii)); cancellation of entire sheets should be communicated in a letter preferably explaining reasons. Claim replacement replaces all earlier claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excluded subject matter from international preliminary examination (Rule 67.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: IPEA is not required to carry out IPE on subject matter that is: (i) scientific and mathematical theories; (ii) plant or animal varieties or essentially biological processes for production of plants/animals (except microbiological processes and their products); (iii) schemes, rules or methods of doing business, performing purely mental acts or playing games; (iv) methods for treatment of the human/animal body by surgery or therapy, and diagnostic methods; (v) mere presentations of information; (vi) computer programs to the extent IPEA is not equipped to examine such programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where such subject matter is present, IPEA may decline to carry out IPE to that extent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure when lack of unity of invention is found (Rule 68.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: If IPEA finds unity of invention requirement not complied with and chooses not to invite restriction or payment of additional fees, it shall proceed with IPE in respect of the entire application but indicate in its written opinion and the report that it considers unity not fulfilled and specify reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPEA can still examine entire application but must expressly record and justify lack of unity in opinion/report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invitation to restrict claims or pay additional fees (Rule 68.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: If IPEA finds lack of unity and chooses to invite the applicant to restrict claims or to pay additional fees, the invitation shall: (i) specify at least one possibility of restriction that would comply; (ii) specify reasons why unity is not complied with; (iii) invite compliance within one month from the date of invitation; (iv) indicate amount of additional fees; (v) invite payment of protest fee (where applicable) within one month and indicate amount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invitation must be specific about restriction options, reasons, fee amounts and deadlines; applicant has one month to act on invitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional fees for lack of unity and protest mechanism (Rule 68.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amount of additional fees due for IPE under Article 34(3)(a) is determined by the competent IPEA and payable directly to it. Applicant may pay additional fees under protest with a reasoned statement asserting compliance with unity or that fee amount is excessive; a review body shall examine protests and may order reimbursement if protest justified. A protest fee may be required; failure to pay the protest fee in time results in protest being considered not made. Review body membership may include the person who made the initial decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protests can result in total or partial reimbursement; text of protest and decision may be notified to elected Offices as annex to the report on applicant request. Protest fee refundable if review body finds protest entirely justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for insufficient restriction and determination of main invention (Rule 68.4–68.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant restricts claims but not sufficiently to comply with unity requirement, IPEA shall proceed as provided in Article 34(3)(c). Where doubt exists as to which invention is main for Article 34(3)(c) purposes, the invention first mentioned in the claims shall be considered the main invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPEA follows Article 34(3)(c) procedures (which may include partial examination) when restriction insufficient; order of claims determines main invention when ambiguous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start of international preliminary examination (Rule 69.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: IPEA shall start IPE when it is in possession of: (i) the demand; (ii) the full amount due for handling and preliminary examination fees (including late payment where applicable); and (iii) either the ISR or an ISA declaration under Article 17(2)(a) that no ISR will be established, and the ISA written opinion under Rule 43 bis.1—unless applicant expressly requests postponement until expiry of the applicable time limit under Rule 54 bis.1(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the same national Office acts as ISA and IPEA, IPE may start at same time as search subject to other conditions; IPEA must also consider statements concerning Article 19/34 amendments that may delay start (see Rule 69.1(c)–(e)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit for establishing the international preliminary examination report (Rule 69.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The time limit for establishing the IPE report is the period which expires last of: (i) 28 months from the priority date; (ii) six months from the time provided under Rule 69.1 for the start of IPE; or (iii) six months from receipt by IPEA of the translation furnished under Rule 55.2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPEA must ensure report is established by the latest of these deadlines; applicants and offices should track priority date, start date and translation receipt to determine applicable deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis, scope and effects to be stated in the international preliminary examination report (Rule 70.1–70.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The report shall mean the international preliminary examination report. It shall issue on the claims as amended (if amended). If report is established as if priority not claimed or if IPEA considers any amendment goes beyond disclosure as filed, the report shall so indicate and give reasons. If parts of the application were not subject to IPE (e.g., no ISR), the report shall indicate this. The report shall indicate whether rectifications of obvious mistakes were taken into account or not, and state whether a top-up search was made (or not) and its date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report must transparently state the factual and procedural basis on which it was prepared (claims version, priority treatment, treatment of amendments, top-up search status, etc.) and provide reasons where it disregards amendments as going beyond the original disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification and dating requirements for the international preliminary examination report (Rule 70.3–70.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report must identify the IPEA which established it (name), the international application (number), the applicant name and the international filing date. It shall indicate the date on which the demand was submitted and the date of the report (date the report is completed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard bibliographic and date information must be present to ensure clarity of the report's provenance and timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification information in the international preliminary examination report (Rule 70.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report shall repeat the classification given under Rule 43.3 if IPEA agrees; otherwise the IPEA shall indicate the classification (at least according to the International Patent Classification) which it considers correct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPEA may change or confirm classification; report must show the classification used for the examination conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement under Article 35(2) in the report (Rule 70.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: The statement referred to in Article 35(2) shall consist of 'YES' or 'NO' (or equivalent) and be accompanied by the citations, explanations and observations referred to in Article 35(2). If any of the three criteria (novelty, inventive step, industrial applicability) is not satisfied the statement shall be negative; if any criterion taken separately is satisfied the report shall specify which criteria are satisfied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The YES/NO statement must be supported by citations and explanations. When negative, the report should still identify any criteria that are satisfied separately, and provide supporting citations/explanations for examiners' conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citations under Article 35(2) (Rule 70.7 reference)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report must provide citations relevant to the Article 35(2) statement (i.e., prior art citations and related explanations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citations should support the IPEA's conclusion on novelty, inventive step and industrial applicability; additional procedural rules for citation presentation are provided in subsequent Rule 70 provisions.
